My wife and I had a very bad experience at this establishment.
I absolutely do not recommend it.

My experience with boarding training was terrible. On his first visit, Mylo went several days without eating. Although I received daily portions of food, I was the one who insisted and asked them to review the situation more closely. Finally, they recommended I pick him up so he could stabilize at home. Mylo returned home underweight, with no appetite, low energy, and almost liquid stools. He also had huge mats in his ears, and his hair had been cut without my permission, a situation the facility itself acknowledged. When I expressed my concern about his condition, I was even told I was a "worry mom."

After several days at home, Mylo regained his appetite and energy. I decided to give the program a second chance and re-enrolled him. A week later, they asked me to pick him up again because he started coughing.

At that time, they told me there were no other dogs with symptoms. Later, during our conversations, they informed me that there were other cases of coughing. That same day, my veterinarian diagnosed a severe respiratory infection that required x-rays, ultrasounds, medication, and nebulizer treatments, resulting in nearly $3,000 in expenses.

After two attempts and approximately two weeks in the program, I completely lost faith in them. I also had no opportunity to assess Mylo's actual training progress, as on both occasions he had to leave the program before the sessions where I was supposed to review his progress with the trainer.
I received neither a full nor a partial refund, nor any support with the veterinary expenses. The alternatives offered were to use their services again and a "Day Pass," something I am no longer willing to do because I have lost faith in their service. (I understand that they make you sign their policies before hiring their service; you sign because you trust that these things won't happen.)
I am sharing my experience so that no one else has to go through something so unpleasant.

I will attach photos of his fur and of the first day he came home after going six days without food.

The third photo of the day, taken after a "cough" turned out to be a severe respiratory infection.
And finally, a photo of Mylo before he went into "training."

Disappointing Experience

I want to share my bad experience with this pet care facility. Although it initially seemed like a good option, the reality was very different.

They asked me to leave my pet for a few hours for a socialization test, which it passed without any problems. However, when they called me to inform me of the result, they told me they wouldn't accept it because it didn't follow instructions and its breed is "very delicate." They also told me that my concern for my pet's well-being was excessive and that they felt "very sorry" but didn't want any problems.

To my surprise, I was able to leave my pet at another place without any problems or excessive requirements. The other place offered excellent service, and I didn't have to go through or pay for a socialization test.

As for the facility itself, I didn't like the lack of transparency in their policies, and asking about the facilities and my pet's well-being worked against them.

An amazing school! They not only focus on having well-behaved dogs, but they also teach you how to understand them and, above all, how to live with them. It's a place you can't help but admire for the respect, affection, and patience they show.

They guide you through the entire process from the moment you first bring your dog in, providing support every step of the way and never leaving you alone.

A great option if it's your first time welcoming a loyal four-legged friend into your family.

The staff is excellent and the security measures are good, but in places like this where you leave your dog as a customer, I recommend checking things like how many dogs they put in a cage and if it gets wet for any reason, like rain or something else, are you sure they dry them off? Or what temperature water they use to bathe them? I hope this recommendation is helpful to you as the dog owner :)

I want to share my experience at Juewoof, not only as a customer but also as someone who loves my dog ​​very much and is quite careful about where I leave her.

I'm always looking for something, from a place that's formal and has clear rules—something that isn't improvised—to one that truly operates responsibly. After all, we're leaving someone who's part of our family.
From the beginning, I appreciated that they explain everything clearly. They talk about the protocols, what can happen when several dogs live together, and how they handle situations like illnesses or fights. You feel like they're not hiding anything from you (which is really appreciated), and on the contrary, they keep you informed, and you even learn things that you, as a pet owner, don't always consider.
Once, my dog ​​got into a fight with another dog, and of course, I was very worried. But I also saw how they handled it and how they kept me informed at all times. Seriously, people, pay close attention to where you take your dogs; it's for their well-being and ours.

In my experience, it's a responsible place and I do recommend it with complete confidence.

My experience was terrible :( My dog ​​was attacked by another dog; his ear, lip, and eye were injured. Then, instead of saying they would take good care of him, they told me they "couldn't guarantee it wouldn't happen again." :( This comment made me feel very uneasy about leaving him there. I believe it's important for dogs to have proper supervision to avoid these situations. This was my personal experience, and I hope it doesn't happen to any other dog. By the way, I should add that the staff at this place sent me messages calling me a "coward" after I posted my review (I have proof). Nothing justifies their neglect of the dogs and these kinds of situations. I'm just sharing my opinion so people can consider it if they want.

My Experience with Chester's Daycare

Taking Chester, my Golden Retriever, to daycare has been one of the best decisions I've ever made. From the very first day, it was clear how happy he was to be there; over time, it has become his safe haven, his second home.

I love seeing how warmly they greet him and how joyfully they say goodbye. It's obvious they love him, and he loves them too. Seeing his excitement every time he arrives is priceless.

The activities they provide and the opportunity to socialize with other dogs have helped him tremendously. Today, Chester is a gentle, sociable, docile, and very well-behaved dog. I'm sure a large part of that is thanks to the positive environment he's found there.

Chester is a sweetheart, and knowing he's in a place where he's cared for and made happy fills me with peace and gratitude.
